h1: The 8 Best Bagged Upright Vacuums for Carpet and Allergy Homes, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Bagged Upright Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 bagged upright vacuums from Kenmore, Oreck, Hoover and Bissell, scored on filtration, brushroll design, weight and bag cost.
summary: The Kenmore Elite 31150 is the best bagged upright for a general home, combining Triple HEPA filtration, a 3D inducer motor and a telescoping wand. The Oreck HEPA is the lighter premium alternative, the Hoover HushTone is the quiet commercial choice, and the Kenmore Intuition with Hair Eliminator brushroll is the value pick for homes with long hair or pets.
intro: Anyone shopping for a bagged upright is usually fighting one of two problems: dust that escapes every time they empty a bin, or a brushroll that clogs with hair. A bag solves the first by sealing what the vacuum picks up. It does nothing for the second, which is why the brushroll and the filter stack matter more than the headline suction claims on the box.

We reviewed eight bagged uprights from their listings and spec sheets, from budget Kenmore Intuition models to commercial Oreck, Hoover and Bissell machines. We ranked them on filtration, brushroll design, weight and handling, and how well each suits a different kind of home. Where a listing gives no weight, motor rating or bag capacity, we say so rather than inventing a number.

products.name: Kenmore Elite 31150 Pet Friendly Bagged Upright Beltless Vacuum w/Pet Handi-Mate, Triple HEPA, 3D Inducer Motor, Telescoping Wand, 5-Position Height Adjustment, 3 Cleaning Tools-Silver
products.verdict: Kenmore's flagship upright, with Triple HEPA filtration, a beltless drive and a telescoping wand.
products.description:
The Elite 31150 is Kenmore's top bagged upright, built around a Triple HEPA filter stack, a 3D inducer motor and a beltless brushroll drive. It adds a telescoping wand, a 5-position height adjustment and a Pet Handi-Mate tool with three cleaning tools.

It ranks first because it is the only machine here that covers filtration, reach and pet use in one package. A beltless drive removes the rubber belt that wears out on conventional uprights, which is the part most owners end up replacing. The five-position height setting lets you move from bare floor to deep rug without hunting for a lever. The tradeoff is that this is the heaviest-feeling and priciest of the Kenmores, and the listing does not publish a weight or bag capacity.

Buy it if the home has pets, carpet and allergy sufferers all in one. Skip it if you want the lightest possible machine for stairs.
cons: Weight and bag size not listed
products.idealFor: Pet owners with carpet and allergy concerns.
products.skipIf: You need the lightest possible upright.

products.name: Oreck HEPA Upright Vacuum Cleaner, Lightweight Bagged Upright Vac
products.verdict: A lightweight bagged upright with HEPA filtration and Oreck's commercial-grade build reputation.
products.description:
The Oreck HEPA is a lightweight bagged upright with HEPA filtration, aimed at buyers who want commercial-grade construction in a home-size machine. Oreck built its name on light uprights that cleaners can carry up and down stairs all day.

It ranks second because it trades the Kenmore Elite's long list of features for a lower weight and a simpler design. For people with bad backs or multi-storey homes, that is a better trade than another attachment. The listing offers no detail on brushroll type, motor power or bag capacity, so we could only rank it on the claims that appear: lightweight, bagged, HEPA. It sits above the Oreck Commercial XL because HEPA matters in a home.

Buy it if you want to carry the vacuum between floors. Skip it if you need a hair-resistant brushroll or a telescoping wand.
pros: HEPA filtration in a light body
products.idealFor: Multi-storey homes where weight is the main concern.
products.skipIf: You want pet-hair tools and a wand.

products.name: Hoover HushTone Commercial Vacuum Cleaner, 13 Inch, Bagged Upright Vac
products.verdict: A 13-inch commercial upright designed to cut noise in offices, hotels and quiet homes.
products.description:
The HushTone is a commercial bagged upright with a 13-inch cleaning path, built to run quietly in places where noise matters. Hoover aims it at offices, hotels and similar spaces, where cleaning happens while people are around.

It ranks third because noise is a real advantage and a rare one in this category, and a 13-inch head is easy to steer through furniture. The cost is a narrower path than a 15-inch machine, so a large room takes more passes, and the listing gives no decibel figure to verify the quiet claim. Compared with the Oreck HEPA it is built for daily commercial use but offers no stated HEPA filtration.

Buy it if you clean around people, such as in an office, a studio or a home with a sleeping baby. Skip it if you need certified HEPA for allergies.
pros: Quiet operation is the design goal
cons: No HEPA claim in the listing
products.idealFor: Offices and homes where noise is a problem.

products.name: Kenmore Intuition Bagged Upright Vacuum with Hair Eliminator Brushroll
products.verdict: A value upright whose Hair Eliminator brushroll is designed to resist wrapping.
products.description:
This Kenmore Intuition model uses a Hair Eliminator brushroll, a design intended to stop hair from winding around the bar. It is a bagged upright in the middle price bracket, below the Elite.

It ranks fourth because hair wrap is the single biggest cause of lost suction in family homes, and fixing it is worth more than another motor spec. A wrapped brushroll forces you to flip the machine and cut hair off with scissors, which is a chore people stop doing. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no filtration or weight details, so there is no basis to claim HEPA, and it ranks below the Hoover on proven build.

Buy it if you have long hair or shedding pets and want a sensible bagged upright. Skip it if allergy filtration is the main reason you are shopping.

products.name: Kenmore Intuition Bagged Upright Vacuum Lift-Up Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: A lift-up design that makes carpeted stairs far easier to reach.
products.description:
The Lift-Up model is a Kenmore Intuition bagged upright designed so the cleaning unit lifts off for hand use. That matters on carpeted stairs, where a full-size upright is awkward and heavy to hold.

It ranks fifth because lift-up designs add a second use to a vacuum that would otherwise only handle floors. The usual weakness is the added complexity: a coupling that has to hold up to repeated clicks, and a hand unit that is heavier than a dedicated hand vacuum. The listing gives no detail on filtration or brushroll type, so we can only point to the lift-up feature itself.

Buy it if your home has carpeted stairs. Skip it if the home is mostly hard floors, where the lift-up is unnecessary.
products.idealFor: Homes with carpeted stairs and few other floors.
products.skipIf: Your home is mostly hard floor.

products.name: Oreck Commercial XL Vacuum Cleaner, Bagged Upright Vac, Lightweight
products.verdict: A light commercial bagged upright without HEPA, for daily cleaning on a budget.
products.description:
The Commercial XL is Oreck's lightweight bagged upright for business use. It is built for daily work, with a simple layout and an emphasis on being easy to carry.

It ranks sixth because it has no filtration claim in the listing and few features beyond the basics. Where it earns its place is simplicity: fewer parts means fewer things to break, and a light body is easier to carry between rooms. Compared with the Oreck HEPA above it, you are giving up filtration in exchange for a lower price bracket.

Buy it if you need a tough, light machine for a shop, office or rental. Skip it if you want HEPA, telescoping reach or pet tools.
products.idealFor: Small businesses and rentals needing a basic machine.
products.skipIf: You want HEPA or pet tools.

products.name: BISSELL BigGreen Commercial PowerForce Bagged Lightweight, Upright, Industrial, Vacuum Cleaner, BGU1451T
products.verdict: An industrial-duty bagged upright built for rental units and janitorial closets.
products.description:
The BigGreen PowerForce BGU1451T is Bissell's commercial bagged upright, described as lightweight and industrial. It targets janitorial and property-management buyers who need a machine that survives rough handling.

It ranks seventh because the BigGreen line is aimed at toughness, not comfort or filtration. The listing gives no HEPA claim and no list of attachments, so it is a cleaning tool rather than a household convenience machine. It comes in below the Oreck Commercial XL only because the Oreck is better known for ease of carrying; both suit similar jobs.

Buy it if you maintain a rental or an office and want a rugged, no-fuss upright. Skip it for a home with allergy needs.
products.idealFor: Rental units and small janitorial jobs.
products.skipIf: You want allergy filtration or tools.

products.name: Kenmore Intuition Bagged Upright Vacuum Cleaner Lightweight
products.verdict: The plainest Kenmore Intuition bagged upright, aimed at buyers who just want it to work.
products.description:
This is the basic Kenmore Intuition bagged upright, described simply as lightweight. It has no brushroll, filtration or lift-up claim to set it apart.

It ranks last because the listing offers nothing beyond the category name, so its case rests on price and familiarity. Kenmore bags and filters are easy to find, which helps ownership costs. The other Intuition models give you a specific benefit, either hair resistance or stair reach, for a similar price bracket.

Buy it if you want the cheapest Kenmore upright and have a simple floor plan. Skip it if hair, pets or allergies are a concern.
products.idealFor: Simple apartments needing a basic vacuum.
products.skipIf: You have pets, long hair or allergies.

methodology.title: Filtration
methodology.description: We compared HEPA claims against listings that give no filtration detail, since a sealed bag is only half of an allergy-friendly system.

methodology.title: Brushroll design
methodology.description: Hair-resistant and beltless drives were weighed against basic brushrolls, because wrap and belt failure are the main owner complaints.

methodology.title: Weight and handling
methodology.description: Lightweight claims, cleaning-path width and lift-up designs were assessed for stairs and multi-room use.

methodology.title: Attachments and reach
methodology.description: Telescoping wands, pet tools and height settings were scored for versatility beyond the main carpet pass.

methodology.title: Ownership cost
methodology.description: Bag availability, bracket price and commercial durability were weighed for long-term value.

whatMatters.detail: A HEPA filter captures very small particles and, with a sealed system, keeps them in the machine. A bag alone only helps at the emptying stage. On a listing, look for HEPA by name and for a sealed system claim, as on the Kenmore Elite and the Oreck HEPA.

A conventional brushroll catches hair and thread, and the bar has to be cut clean. Hair-resistant designs, such as the Hair Eliminator on the Intuition model, shed hair toward the intake. Beltless drives remove the belt entirely, which is the part owners replace most.

An upright that you dread lifting does not get used. Lightweight models like the Oreck units are easier up stairs, while feature-rich machines carry heavier motors. Always check whether the listing gives a weight figure, and be careful where it does not.

Multi-position height settings let the head ride across bare floor, thin rugs and deep carpet. A telescoping wand extends reach for ceilings and furniture. The Kenmore Elite offers both; most budget models offer neither.

Bags are the running cost of this category. Branded Kenmore, Oreck and Hoover bags are easy to find, but they vary in price. Check the bag type before buying, and avoid unusual formats you cannot restock easily.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: HEPA filtration stated by name, a sealed system and a bagged design so you never touch loose dust at emptying time.

cards.text: The Kenmore Elite 31150 has Triple HEPA, and the Oreck HEPA Upright offers HEPA in a lighter body. Models without a filtration claim should not be assumed to be HEPA.

cards.text: You have pets, allergies, or carpet through most of the house. The Kenmore Elite and Oreck HEPA justify the extra.

faq.q: Are bagged uprights better than bagless?
faq.a: For dust control, yes. A bag seals what you pick up so you never tip a dirty bin, which matters for allergies. The tradeoff is the recurring cost of bags.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a bagged upright?
faq.a: Assuming bagged means HEPA. Many listings, including several here, give no filtration detail. If allergies matter, buy a model that states HEPA, such as the Kenmore Elite or Oreck HEPA.

faq.q: Is the Kenmore Elite worth it over an Intuition?
faq.a: If you have pets and carpet, yes. The beltless drive, Triple HEPA and telescoping wand add up to a longer-lasting machine. For a small flat or light use, the Intuition is enough.

faq.q: How often should I change the bag?
faq.a: Change it when it is about two thirds full, not when it is packed. A full bag chokes airflow and weakens cleaning. Replace the filters on the schedule in the manual.
Most can, if you switch off the brushroll or raise the height setting. The Kenmore Elite's five-position adjustment helps here. Machines without a height setting may scatter debris on hard floors.

faq.q: Can a lift-up model replace a hand vacuum?
faq.a: For stairs and car seats, yes. The lift-up Kenmore Intuition works well on carpeted steps, though the removable unit is heavier than a dedicated handheld.

finalTake: For most homes, the Kenmore Elite 31150 is the bagged upright to buy, with Triple HEPA, a beltless drive and a telescoping wand. The Oreck HEPA is the better choice if weight is your main worry, and the Hoover HushTone suits quiet commercial use. The Kenmore Intuition with Hair Eliminator brushroll is the value pick for long hair, while the Oreck Commercial XL and Bissell BigGreen are for rugged jobs. Check the listing for a HEPA claim before you assume it.
